turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your inquiries into my motivations are irrelevant, Sandip. I am concerned with the well-being of those under my care, and your actions are demonstrably causing them distress. Let us be clear: my request for you to leave is not a suggestion, but a directive.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, a *directive*, is it? How very... Roman of you, Nikhil. It seems the weight of empire rests heavily on your shoulders, though I suspect it's more a performance than a reality, wouldn't you agree?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your attempts at mockery are tiresome, Sandip. I am not concerned with your assessment of my actions, only with the consequences of them. Consider this your final warning.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: A final warning, you say? How delightfully dramatic, Nikhil. One might almost believe you're channeling Lear, railing against the storm – though, of course, your storm is merely a few disgruntled peasants, and your kingdom, a rather modest estate.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your theatricality is unnecessary, Sandip. I understand you seek to unsettle me, but I will not indulge your games. Address your concerns directly, or consider this conversation concluded.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Concluded, you say? Such a swift dismissal, Nikhil. It reminds me of Prospero, abruptly abandoning his enchanted isle - a retreat born, I suspect, of a certain... discomfort. Perhaps you fear the echoes of unrest that gather beyond your manicured lawns?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip's allusions are frivolous and serve no purpose. If you possess genuine concerns regarding unrest, present them with clarity and substance, rather than resorting to literary comparisons. Otherwise, I suggest you depart.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Clarity and substance, you demand? How very…pedestrian, Nikhil. It seems the weight of responsibility has dulled your perception, leaving you blind to the subtle currents swirling around us – currents that, I assure you, are far more potent than any unruly peasant. Let us speak, then, of the whispers carried on the wind, the fervor of those men who preach a different kind of justice, a justice that does not bow to landed gentry.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your attempts at intimidation are transparent, Sandip. These 'whispers' you describe are easily traced to those who seek to exploit division for their own gain. I am not blind to the complexities of the situation, but I will not be swayed by fear-mongering.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Fear-mongering, you call it? A rather convenient label, isn’t it, Nikhil? It allows one to dismiss inconvenient truths with such effortless grace, much like a magician diverting attention with a flourish. Tell me, are you truly so certain your walls, however grand, can contain the tide of conviction that is rising?

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: The air grows thick, doesn't it? Such pronouncements…they carry a certain weight, a heaviness that settles not just upon Nikhil, but upon us all.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Indeed, Bimala, a heaviness. One might even say a premonition, wouldn't you agree, Nikhil? It reminds me of Cassandra's curse, you see – to foresee the ruin of Troy, yet be forever disbelieved. A tragic fate, wouldn’t you say, for one so…perceptive?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your allusions to Greek mythology are, as always, theatrical, Sandip. I am not concerned with prophecies, but with tangible realities and the well-being of those under my care. Let us dispense with the veiled pronouncements and address any specific concerns you may have, if they are genuinely intended for my ears.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Tangible realities, you say? A charmingly bourgeois sentiment, Nikhil. But tell me, are those realities truly so…stable, so impervious to the subtle shifts in the wind? I merely observe, you see, like a naturalist cataloging the approaching storm.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your observations, Sandip, are noted, but lack substance. I am familiar with the patterns of weather, both meteorological and societal; speculation does not constitute a forecast. If you possess information regarding genuine threats, present it directly, rather than employing such elaborate metaphors.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, 'substance,' Nikhil. Such a…demanding word. Perhaps you mistake my literary flourishes for mere affectation; I assure you, I find the human condition quite ripe for metaphorical exploration, especially when observing those who cling so tightly to their perceived stability. Let us just say, I've heard whispers, unsettling murmurs, of certain…zealous preachers gaining traction amongst the populace, and their interpretations of piety are…less than conducive to a peaceful co-existence.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: The preachers…their fervor is certainly…noticeable. One hopes their convictions do not overshadow reason, Nikhil. But Sandip speaks of whispers; are these truly matters for concern, or merely echoes of discontent?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Bimala's concern is understandable, but I share her hope for reason to prevail. I will investigate these preachers and their influence, Sandip, but I require specifics, not pronouncements of impending doom. Let us not mistake agitation for genuine threat; I am not easily swayed by conjecture.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Specifics, you demand, Nikhil? As if the universe operates with the precision of your meticulously managed estates! Very well, let us consider the subtle erosion of faith, the insidious appeal to the dispossessed - these are the seeds from which genuine unrest blossoms, and they rarely announce themselves with trumpets and banners.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip’s analogy is predictably grandiose, and demonstrably unhelpful. I am not unaware of the grievances harbored within the community; my responsibility extends to addressing them fairly, not reacting to hyperbolic pronouncements. Let us move past these artistic digressions and address the matter at hand – if there is one.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ...

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
